steps.observation: You have 30 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
DNA  
• Sugar: Deoxyribose (no oxygen on 2′ carbon).  
• Bases: A, T, C, G.  
• Structure: Usually double-stranded helix.  
• Stability: Chemically more stable; good for long-term information storage.  
• Main role: Permanent genetic blueprint; replicated and passed to offspring; mostly confined to nucleus in eukaryotes.

RNA  
• Sugar: Ribose (has oxygen on 2′ carbon).  
• Bases: A, U, C, G (uracil replaces thymine).  
• Structure: Usually single-stranded; can fold into complex shapes.  
• Stability: Less stable and shorter-lived.  
• Main roles: Working copies and tools—mRNA carries instructions, rRNA and tRNA build proteins, plus many regulatory types; found in nucleus, cytoplasm, and elsewhere.

In short: DNA is the durable archive; RNA is the versatile, short-term working copy and machinery.
